hypotheses.justification: The statement only needs `[Field K]`. Mathlib defines `InfiniteAdeleRing (K : Type*) [Field K]`, and its `CommRing` instance is derived with only `[Field K]` (`deriving CommRing, ...`). `unipotentGL2` (defined for `{R} [CommRing R]` in Def_AutomorphicForm_ConstantTerm), `diagUnits2` (defined for `{A} [CommRing A]` in Def_LanglandsTunnell_CubicInduction_TorusValues), `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.scalar` and the group structure on `GL (Fin 2) _` all need only a commutative ring. So the statement elaborates without `NumberField K`; it is only pulled in as an instance-implicit section variable. The claim is a matrix identity that holds over any commutative ring, so it stays true, including when the ring is trivial. The proof uses the local helper lemmas `unipotentGL2_inv`, `scalar_mul_diagUnits2` and `diagUnits2_val'`. These carry `[NumberField K]` only because they are in the same section; their proofs (`Units.ext`, `diagUnits2_val`/`coe_diagUnits2`, `Matrix.diagonal_mul_diagonal`, `fin_cases` and `simp`) are pure ring computations that never use `NumberField`. The fix is to restate them with `omit [NumberField K] in`, or to inline the same computation. The remaining steps (`Units.ext`, `ext`/`fin_cases`/`simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two]`, and `linear_combination` with `Units.mul_inv u`) work in any commutative ring.
